stories.title: Tether Wants Its Gold Token to Rival ETFs
stories.summary: Tether wants its gold-backed token to compete with gold ETFs, CryptoSlate reports. The report frames this as a goal, not a launched product. It gives no data on the token's size or trading volume.
stories.whyItMatters: A gold token that rivals ETFs could draw capital from traditional funds into crypto markets.
whatToWatch: Watch for data on the token's holdings and trading volume.
Watch for reaction from ETF providers or regulators.
questions: How is the token's gold backing verified?
How big is the token's market today?

sources.title: Tether wants its gold token to rival ETFs

stories.title: Holding $10,000 in Stablecoins Would Have Gained €420 — Without Interest
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis says $10,000 held in stablecoins would have gained €420 in value. The gain came from currency moves between the dollar and the euro. It did not come from interest on the stablecoins. The analysis gives no further detail on the time period used.
stories.whyItMatters: This shows stablecoins can offer a currency hedge for euro-based holders, beyond the debate over stablecoin yield.
whatToWatch: Watch EU rules on stablecoins and currency exposure.
Watch the dollar-euro exchange rate trend.
questions: What time period does this analysis cover?
Does the figure include fees or slippage?

sources.title: How $10,000 in stablecoins would have gained €420 without earning interest

stories.title: Bitcoin Looks Cheap by One Measure After $1 Billion in ETF Outflows
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1 billion in outflows, CryptoSlate reports. Despite this, one valuation measure now shows Bitcoin as cheap. The report does not name the measure or give a time frame for the outflows.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows signal institutional sentiment, so outflows next to a 'cheap' reading matter for investors watching entry points.
whatToWatch: Watch for further ETF flow data in coming days.
Watch whether outflows reverse or continue.
questions: Which valuation measure is used here?
Over what period did the $1 billion outflow happen?

sources.title: Bitcoin now looks cheap by one measure after $1 billion in ETF outflows

stories.title: Is Ethereum the 'Worst Asset of All Time'? BitMine's Loss Fuels the Debate
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate piece asks whether Ethereum is the 'worst asset of all time.' It cites an estimated $8.83 billion loss tied to BitMine's Ethereum holdings. The claim is posed as a question, not a confirmed finding. The source gives no detail on how the loss figure was calculated.
stories.whyItMatters: Large paper losses at a corporate Ethereum holder raise questions about risk management in crypto treasury strategies.
whatToWatch: Watch for BitMine disclosures on its Ethereum position.
Watch Ethereum's price for further swings.
questions: Is the $8.83 billion loss realized or unrealized?
What method produced this loss estimate?

sources.title: Is Ethereum the “worst asset of all time,” amid estimated $8.83 billion BitMine loss ?

stories.title: Britain's £4 Billion Grid Fix: Could Bitcoin Miners Use the Wasted Wind?
stories.summary: Britain plans to spend £4 billion on grid bottlenecks, CryptoSlate reports. The piece asks whether Bitcoin miners could use curtailed wind power that otherwise goes to waste. This is framed as a question, not an announced plan. No specific project or timeline is given.
stories.whyItMatters: Pairing Bitcoin mining with curtailed renewable power could reshape the debate over mining's energy use.
whatToWatch: Watch for any UK pilot linking miners to curtailed wind power.
Watch the grid investment timeline.
questions: Is any miner or utility planning this now?
What approval would such a project need?

sources.title: Britain to spend £4 billion on grid bottlenecks. Can Bitcoin use the wasted wind?

stories.title: The Fed's Bond Market Rescue Could Still Hurt Bitcoin
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate piece says the Federal Reserve could act to support bond markets. The same action may create headwinds for Bitcoin. The source gives no specific Fed policy or date.
stories.whyItMatters: Fed liquidity moves shape risk appetite across markets, including Bitcoin, so this tension matters for investors sizing exposure.
whatToWatch: Watch upcoming Fed meetings and statements.
Watch bond market stress indicators.
questions: What specific Fed action is under discussion?
How would it affect Bitcoin's price?

sources.title: The Fed could rescue bond markets and still make life harder for Bitcoin

stories.title: Robots Run AI-Written Code on Their Own, Succeed 92% of the Time
stories.summary: A new report says robots can run AI-written code without an AI directing each step. The tests succeeded 92% of the time. The report frames this as a step toward more autonomous robotics. It gives no detail on the test setup or sample size.
stories.whyItMatters: Autonomous AI systems in physical robots raise oversight questions that echo broader worries about unsupervised code execution.
whatToWatch: Watch for published details on the test method.
Watch for any safety incidents tied to autonomous runs.
questions: What counted as success in this test?
Who conducted the research?

sources.title: Robots now run AI-written code without an AI calling the shots, succeeding 92% of the time

stories.title: Lido's Lending Plan Could Block Repayments While Interest Still Accrues
stories.summary: Lido's proposed lending plan could stop borrowers from repaying loans in some cases, CryptoSlate reports. Interest would keep accruing even when repayment is blocked. The piece presents this as a design risk, not a live incident. Details of the plan's mechanics are limited in the source.
stories.whyItMatters: Lido is a major liquid-staking protocol, so a flaw here could affect ETH staking yields and trust across DeFi.
whatToWatch: Watch for Lido's response or a plan revision.
Watch for a governance vote on the proposal.
questions: Has Lido's team confirmed this flaw?
How many users or how much value is at risk?

sources.title: Lido’s lending plan could block loan repayments without stopping interest

stories.title: AI Models Agreed With Each Other More Than With Reality, Test Finds
stories.summary: A new test found that AI models agreed with each other more than they matched factual reality, CryptoSlate reports. This points to a kind of groupthink among AI systems. The source does not name the models tested or describe the method used.
stories.whyItMatters: Crypto research and trading tools increasingly use AI, so models that converge on errors rather than facts are a real risk.
whatToWatch: Watch for the full study and its methodology.
Watch for follow-up tests on other models.
questions: Which AI models were tested?
How did the test define 'reality'?

sources.title: AI models agreed with each other more than with reality in a new test

stories.title: AI Helped Hackers Breach 10 Unnamed Organizations, Researchers Say
stories.summary: Researchers say AI tools helped hackers gain access to systems at 10 unnamed organizations, CryptoSlate reports. Neither the organizations nor the researchers are named in the available source. The report gives no detail on the attack methods used.
stories.whyItMatters: AI-assisted attacks threaten exchanges, custodians, and other crypto infrastructure that depend on strong security.
whatToWatch: Watch for disclosure of the affected organizations or sectors.
Watch for the researchers' full report.
questions: Were any crypto firms among the 10 organizations?
What AI capability did the attackers use?

sources.title: AI helped hackers gain access at 10 unnamed organizations, researchers say
